Working closely with network architects, senior engineers, and IT leadership, this position helps maintain reliable and scalable network services across the university. The Network Engineer position supports the deployment, troubleshooting, lifecycle management, and daily operation of enterprise network infrastructure, including switching, routing, wireless, firewalls, network monitoring, automation platforms, and related services such as IP addressing, VLANs, DHCP, DNS, and campus connectivity. The position contributes to project implementation, operational support, documentation, and continuous improvement efforts supporting enterprise network services. Network Implementation and Engineering Support: Assist with the installation, configuration, testing, validation, and maintenance of network hardware, software, and related infrastructure. Participate in network upgrades, lifecycle replacements, hardware refreshes, scheduled maintenance activities, and implementation of approved network standards and configuration baselines. Collaborate with team members, customers, vendors, and technology partners to support infrastructure projects, service improvements, and completed change validation. Evaluate and test new tools, technologies, and operational improvements. Foster productive working relationships through professional, customer-focused interactions and collaboration with engineers and leadership. Support operating system modernization, technology refresh, and lifecycle activities while maintaining approved operational, security, and compliance configurations. Validate server health, application connectivity, and stability after maintenance; resolve package, repository, dependency, kernel, boot, and configuration failures. Remediate vulnerabilities and maintain procedures, records, evidence, and documentation supporting cybersecurity requirements and applicable SOX and NERC CIP controls. Automation and Infrastructure as Code Develop, test, maintain, and support Ansible playbooks, roles, inventories, templates, and workflows for provisioning, patching, configuration, compliance, and maintenance. Use Bash, Python, or similar scripting to reduce manual work and improve consistency; contribute to Infrastructure as Code using technologies such as Terraform. Maintain automation in approved source control and apply appropriate safeguards, validation, error handling, and controlled execution. Incident and Operational Support Diagnose and resolve complex Linux incidents, service requests, and escalations, including high-priority production events and live troubleshooting calls. Perform root cause analysis and recommend corrective and preventive actions for issues involving performance, connectivity, DNS, storage, authentication, services, packages, and application dependencies. Create and maintain runbooks, troubleshooting guides, operational procedures, and technical documentation; participate in on-call support and planned maintenance. Security, Cloud, and Platform Support Apply Linux hardening standards and secure configuration practices; support access management, privileged-account controls, audits, evidence collection, and remediation activities. Support Linux systems across on-premises, VMware, and cloud environments, preferably Microsoft Azure or AWS, including compute, storage, networking, DNS, and identity dependencies. Provide operational support and cross-platform troubleshooting for containerized workloads and related infrastructure when required. Collaboration and Knowledge Transfer Coordinate effectively across Infrastructure Operations, Cybersecurity, Application Support, Database, Network, Monitoring, and Cloud Engineering. Communicate technical issues, risks, status, and recommendations clearly; share knowledge, provide hands-on knowledge transfer, and participate in reviews, planning, change management, and continuous improvement. Required Years of Experience: 5+ years of hands-on enterprise Linux administration experience Education: Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science or Computer Engineering

Support core AVD operational components (host pools/session hosts, scaling, image lifecycle, and operational troubleshooting) as part of day-to-day support. Contribute to runbooks, SOPs, and operational documentation to increase repeatability and reduce operational risk. Demonstrated hands-on experience with Azure IaaS operations (VMs, resource organization, standard operational tooling). Operational disciplines: incident/change management, documentation, and service delivery. Experience with Azure NetApp Files, performance tiers/service levels, snapshots, troubleshooting and replication concepts. Experience supporting Azure VMs and AVD environments. Familiarity with Azure RBAC concepts and standard built-in roles. Certificates, Licenses, And/or Registrations Preferred Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) Microsoft Certified: Azure Virtual Desktop Specialty (AZ-140) Microsoft Certified: Azure Network Engineer Associate (AZ-700) Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator Associate (SC-300) Microsoft Certified: Azure Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500) NetApp Certified Cloud and Storage Services Engineer Professional (NS0-701) Pre-employment drug screening and background check are conditions of employment.
